name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,839

entries.clue: Assemble trick grid which possibly splits (10)

indicatorNotes.splits: a thing that splits comes apart in the middle, and the two letters named just after it drop into the gap that opens

blocks.note: a con is a trick, the swindler's kind
a grate is the grid of iron bars in a fireplace
possibly marks what follows as an instance, and 'for example' is written eg

annotation.surface: A trick grid that might just come apart in the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Assemble' sits exactly where an anagram indicator usually sits, and it is the definition. Eg for 'possibly' is worth filing away: 'say', 'perhaps' and 'possibly' all summon those two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Assemble -> CONGREGATE: both verbs mean to gather into one place, congregate being what a crowd does of its own accord.

entries.clue: Rough like sensei's blows? (6)

blocks.note: the sea sense: short broken waves rather than a smooth swell
a sensei is a martial arts teacher, and what he deals out are chops

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether a thing is as rough as a karate teacher's strikes.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark is the setter admitting the second definition is a coinage: nobody calls a dojo choppy until this clue does. Water is where the word normally lives.
annotation.definitionFit: Rough -> CHOPPY: a choppy sea is rough with short broken waves; and since a sensei's blows are chops, anything made of chops is choppy.

entries.clue: African Queen worked free in time, then it capsized (9)

indicatorNotes.worked: dough that is worked is pushed out of shape over and over, and letters worked the same way come out in a new order
indicatorNotes.capsized: a boat that capsizes turns right over, so in a down clue the letters named are written bottom to top

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters taken as they stand
t = time, as on a stopwatch, and it joins the fodder
IT written upwards

annotation.surface: An African monarch freeing up some time, until her boat turned over.
annotation.walkthrough: Nefertiti was queen of Egypt beside Akhenaten in the fourteenth century BC, and Egypt is in Africa. The Bogart film is the decoy the capsizing plays to.
annotation.definitionFit: African Queen -> NEFERTITI: one named queen standing in for the class, Egypt's most famous, from a continent the surface would rather you read as a film title.

entries.clue: Agency helping to keep European here (14)

indicatorNotes.to keep: what you keep you hold on to, so these letters close around the pieces named after them

blocks.note: a helping doled out is a ration
e is the usual short form of European
answer to your name at register and you are present

annotation.surface: An agency working to keep a European resident in the country.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is one word at the head of a fourteen-letter answer, which is where the difficulty sits. 'Here' is the school register sense, and a helping of anything is a ration.
annotation.definitionFit: Agency -> REPRESENTATION: an agency acts on someone else's behalf, and representation is that acting-for, as an actor signs with an agency to get it.

entries.clue: Eccentric left collection of animals with tails removed (5)

indicatorNotes.with tails removed: an animal's tail is at its back end, so each word named loses its final letter

blocks.note: left in the sense of departed is GONE, docked of its E
a zoo is a collection of animals, docked of one O

annotation.surface: An oddball walked out on a menagerie of animals that had been docked.
annotation.walkthrough: Gonzo is Hunter S. Thompson's word for reporting that puts the reporter in the story, and it has drifted to mean simply bizarre. 'Left' is the past tense of leave, not the opposite of right.
annotation.definitionFit: Eccentric -> GONZO: gonzo describes the wild, rule-breaking and off-kilter, the adjective having spread from Thompson's journalism to anything odd.

entries.clue: Youth I see across stage attractive on set (9)

indicatorNotes.across: one thing laid across another spans it and covers it, so the letters named first go round the ones named last

blocks.note: a youth is a teen
I stands for itself and C is the letter whose name is said 'see'
a leg of a race or a tour is one stage of it

annotation.surface: A young person I can pick out across the stage, good-looking under the lights.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' is the television studio's, which is what lets a three-word definition hide at the end of the sentence. A leg of a journey is a stage of it.
annotation.definitionFit: attractive on set -> TELEGENIC: someone telegenic looks good on camera, television's counterpart to photogenic.

entries.clue: Remaining piece put back however small (4)

indicatorNotes.put back: what is put back returns the way it came, so the letters named next are read from their far end

blocks.note: however and but make the same turn in a sentence
s = small, from the clothing label

annotation.surface: Returning a leftover scrap to where it came from, no matter how little is left.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a note about tidying up, 'however small' the concession at the end. A stub is what survives of a ticket, a cheque or a pencil once the rest has gone.
annotation.definitionFit: Remaining piece -> STUB: the short end left behind when the rest has been torn off or used up, as with a ticket stub.

entries.clue: Worry the top comes off lock (5)

indicatorNotes.the top comes off: in a down answer the top is the first letter, and a top that comes off leaves the word one letter shorter

blocks.note: worry is STRESS, here without the S at its head

annotation.surface: Anxiety that the top of a lock is about to come away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lock' is hair rather than hardware: a tress is a long lock of it, and the clue leans on the other sense from end to end. In a down clue a word's top is its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: lock -> TRESS: a tress is a long lock of hair, lock being the everyday word for the same hank.

entries.clue: Radiation unintentionally reveals the inside of car parts (4,4)

indicatorNotes.the inside of: the inside of a word is the letter at its centre, with the rest of it packed either side
indicatorNotes.parts: to part is to come apart in the middle, so the letters before open up and let the next one in

blocks.note: to betray a secret is to give it away without meaning to
the middle letter of CAR

annotation.surface: Radiation accidentally showing up what is inside a car's components.
annotation.walkthrough: Beta rays are the electrons flung out by a decaying nucleus, the middle member of alpha, beta and gamma. 'Parts' looks like the car's components and is a verb telling one word to open.
annotation.definitionFit: Radiation -> BETA RAYS: the stream of electrons a radioactive nucleus emits, one of the three named kinds of radiation.

entries.clue: OTT style Colin developed with drag queen (14)

indicatorNotes.developed: what is developed is worked up into a shape it did not have before, and these letters change the same way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, five letters
anagram fodder, nine more

annotation.surface: Colin working up an extravagant new look as a drag queen.
annotation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for over the top, in use since the 1980s. All fourteen letters lie in plain sight, and the Q is the one to count first.
annotation.definitionFit: OTT style -> GRANDILOQUENCE: language pitched far higher than the occasion asks for, all grand words and flourishes.

entries.clue: Sort of ball hits leg (3-4)

blocks.note: in gangland slang to off a man is to kill him, so hits are offs
pins are legs, as in being unsteady on your pins

annotation.surface: A delivery of some kind striking the batsman on the leg.
annotation.walkthrough: Off-spin is the bowling that turns in towards the batsman from the off side, so the cricket surface and the answer share a world. Both wordplay words are slang instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Sort of ball -> OFF-SPIN: in cricket a ball is one delivery, and off-spin names the type that turns from the off side towards leg.

entries.clue: Glass of beer drunk by Spooner to celebrate (5,2)

indicatorNotes.by Spooner: the Reverend Spooner was the Oxford don whose tongue traded the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the two named here swap their fronts

blocks.note: a jar is a glass of beer and lit means drunk; trade the J and the L at the front and 'jar lit' comes out as these letters

annotation.surface: The Reverend Spooner sinking a glass of beer by way of celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: To large it is British slang for going out and celebrating hard, heard from the 1990s on. 'Drunk' is the state rather than the verb, which is where the sounding starts.
annotation.definitionFit: to celebrate -> LARGE IT: British slang for going out and enjoying yourself without restraint, usually heard as larging it.

entries.clue: Small clean trousers wrinkle (5)

indicatorNotes.trousers: to trouser something is to pocket it, and what is pocketed vanishes inside

blocks.note: clean in the sense of unpolluted is pure
s = small, from the clothing label

annotation.surface: A small clean pair of trousers with a crease across them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is a verb here — to trouser the takings is to pocket them — which is how a garment comes to hold a letter. Lips wrinkle by pursing.
annotation.definitionFit: wrinkle -> PURSE: to purse the lips is to draw them into wrinkles, both verbs naming the same gathering up of skin.

entries.clue: Runner with hoop earrings jogged (9)

indicatorNotes.jogged: to jog a thing is to knock it out of place, and letters knocked about like that settle in a new order

blocks.note: a hoop is a ring, the shape of the letter O
anagram fodder, eight letters

annotation.surface: A runner in hoop earrings out for a jog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jogged' does double duty: it is the runner's own word and the instruction to shake the letters up. The person who runs a thing runs it in the managing sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Runner -> ORGANISER: the one who runs a festival, a raffle or a race is its organiser, running there meaning managing rather than sprinting.

entries.clue: Cheap wine not opened by thoughtful lady on vacation (13)

annotation.definitionNote: Cheap doubles as an adverb in English — you can buy a thing cheap, or get away cheap — so it stands in for the -ly word.

indicatorNotes.not opened: the opener of a word is its first letter, and a word that is not opened has to do without it
indicatorNotes.on vacation: a house whose owners are on vacation stands empty, so the word named keeps only its outside and loses everything between

blocks.note: WINE with its opening W gone
a room ten by twelve is written 10 x 12, so by is that sign
pensive is thoughtful, lost in thought
LADY emptied out, keeping only its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A thoughtful woman away on holiday with a bottle of cheap wine still corked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' as the multiplication sign is the piece to keep: a plot twelve by twenty is 12 x 20. Two different emptyings sit side by side, one taking a head and one taking a middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheap -> INEXPENSIVELY: both say a thing cost little, cheap serving as the adverb in phrases like bought it cheap.

entries.clue: Grant's brother and 'is woman play around (9)

blocks.note: Phil and Grant Mitchell are the brothers at the centre of the BBC soap EastEnders
the connective taken as letters
a woman is HER, and the dropped aitch of 'is says to drop this one too

annotation.surface: One of the Mitchell brothers and his girlfriend messing about.
annotation.walkthrough: Phil and Grant Mitchell have been EastEnders' feuding hard men since 1990, and that soap is the only place this Grant lives. The apostrophe is an instruction rather than decoration: an aitch has already gone, and another goes the same way.
annotation.definitionFit: play around -> PHILANDER: to philander is to carry on with people you have made no commitment to, which is what playing around means of a partner.

entries.clue: Conductor designate travelled by bike (9)

blocks.note: the president elect is the one designated, chosen and waiting to start
you ride a bike, so yesterday you rode it

annotation.surface: An orchestra's incoming conductor cycling to rehearsal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' is the electrical sort, the terminal current passes through, and the orchestra is there to keep you from seeing it. Designate and elect are the same word in titles like president elect.
annotation.definitionFit: Conductor -> ELECTRODE: an electrode is the conductor by which current enters or leaves a battery, a valve or a body.

entries.clue: Name large dog that pirouettes after Nureyev, perhaps (8)

indicatorNotes.that pirouettes: a pirouette is a dancer's spin on the spot, and letters spun like that come out the other way round

blocks.note: to cite someone is to name them
l = large, the shirt size
a lab is a Labrador

annotation.surface: Naming a big dog that spins about the way Nureyev used to.
annotation.walkthrough: Rudolf Nureyev was the Kirov's star who defected to the West in 1961, and he belongs to the definition rather than the wordplay. 'After' means in the style of, as a painting is after Rembrandt.
annotation.definitionFit: after Nureyev, perhaps -> BALLETIC: after in the sense of in the manner of, with the 'perhaps' marking one dancer as the example of the art the word describes.

entries.clue: Celebrity chef on broadcast filling in met old BBC correspondent (8,5)

indicatorNotes.on: across the grid one thing sits on another by following it, so the chef's letters go after the broadcast's
indicatorNotes.filling in: the filling in a word is what sits at its centre, the letter with the rest packed round it

blocks.note: the A-list is where the famous are ranked
to air a programme is to broadcast it
a chef is a cook
the middle letter of MET

annotation.surface: A famous chef standing in on a broadcast once met a veteran BBC reporter.
annotation.walkthrough: Alistair Cooke sent Letter from America to the BBC every week from 1946 until weeks before his death in 2004. 'Filling in' looks like the deputising the chef is doing and asks for a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: old BBC correspondent -> ALISTAIR COOKE: the Anglo-American journalist whose weekly Letter from America explained the United States to BBC radio for fifty-eight years.

entries.clue: Not all Gestapo interrogations done nicely (1,5)

indicatorNotes.Not all: taking not all of something is taking a part of it, and the part wanted is a run of letters lying in the open

blocks.note: GestAPO INTerrogations carries the letters in order across the join

annotation.surface: Questioning by the Gestapo that was not, on the whole, politely done.
annotation.walkthrough: À point is the kitchen's French for meat cooked exactly right, and it turns up on English menus. The run crosses the gap between two words, which is where hiding works best.
annotation.definitionFit: done nicely -> A POINT: done is cooked, and à point is the degree at which a steak is cooked just so, neither under nor over.

entries.clue: Field remains full of wheat, initially at any rate (9)

indicatorNotes.full of: what is full of a thing has that thing inside it, so the letter named next goes within the letters before
indicatorNotes.initially: an initial is the first letter of a word, and initially asks for that letter on its own

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow, the poetic and old word for a field
whatever remains stays
the first letter of WHEAT

annotation.surface: A field of stubble still full of wheat, or so the farmer says.
annotation.walkthrough: Leastways is colloquial and dialect for 'at least', the word a character in a novel uses to soften what they have just said. Lea earns its keep in grids: three letters, two of them vowels.
annotation.definitionFit: at any rate -> LEASTWAYS: a dialect form of 'at least', used exactly as 'at any rate' is, to qualify the statement just made.

entries.clue: Party in a navy dress (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in puts the party's letters inside, between the two pieces named after it

blocks.note: the article taken as it stands
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's senior service
a do is a party, as in a works do

annotation.surface: Someone turning up to a party in a navy dress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Navy' is a colour on the surface and the Royal Navy underneath, and 'dress' is the verb that defines. A do is British for any party at all: an office do, a leaving do.
annotation.definitionFit: dress -> ADORN: to dress a shop window or a Christmas tree is to adorn it, both verbs meaning to deck a thing out.

entries.clue: Ecuador's capital no longer safe around clubs (5)

indicatorNotes.around: what goes around a thing encircles it, so the letters named first close over the one named after

blocks.note: safe in the sense of certain is sure — a safe bet is a sure thing
c is clubs on a bridge scorecard

annotation.surface: A capital city that has lost its safety, ringed by nightclubs.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital is money here, not a city: the sucre was Ecuador's currency until the country changed to the US dollar in 2000. Sucre is also the capital of Bolivia, which is the trap the clue sets.
annotation.definitionFit: Ecuador's capital no longer -> SUCRE: capital in the money sense, the sucre having been Ecuador's currency until dollarisation retired it.

entries.clue: Presumably nothing from Q in your mind (2,3)

blocks.note: cut the alphabet off before Q and the run that survives reaches only as far as its sixteenth letter

annotation.surface: Someone guessing that nothing beginning with Q has stayed in your memory.
annotation.walkthrough: The alphabet is the whole of the wordplay, and Q's place in it is all the clue needs. Up top is the British idiom for the head, as in not much up top.
annotation.definitionFit: in your mind -> UP TOP: up top is the head, the top storey where the thinking is done, as in being sharp up top.

entries.clue: Binary judgment's backing women as they were long ago (7)

indicatorNotes.backing: a thing's backing is what sits at its back, so only the letter at the end of the word named is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of JUDGMENT
w = women, as on the lavatory door
of old means as things stood in the past

annotation.surface: A court ruling that comes out in support of women as they used to be.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as support and asks for a last letter instead. Of old survives in phrases like a friend of old, meaning from the far past.
annotation.definitionFit: Binary -> TWOFOLD: both adjectives say a thing comes in two parts, binary being the technical word and twofold the plain one.

entries.clue: £1 for the last of 26 Italian pastries (7)

indicatorNotes.for the last of: for means in place of here, and the last of a word is its final letter, so that letter steps aside for the piece named first

blocks.note: 26 across answers CAN'T, which written out in full is CANNOT, and that word gives up its final letter
l is the pound, from the Latin libra the £ sign is drawn from, and i is Roman one

annotation.surface: A pound each for the last of the Italian pastries in the tray.
annotation.walkthrough: Cannoli are the Sicilian tubes of fried pastry piped full of sweetened ricotta. The chain runs through the long form: 26's answer is the contraction, and it is CANNOT that loses its letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Italian pastries -> CANNOLI: the plural of cannolo, the Sicilian pastry tubes filled with sweetened ricotta.

entries.clue: Lack the strength to lean over (4)

annotation.definitionNote: The first definition wants CAN'T; grids have no squares for apostrophes, so the entry goes in as four plain letters.

blocks.note: the shortened form of 'cannot', said whenever the ability is missing
the builder's and sailor's verb for tilting off the vertical, as a ship does in a swell

annotation.surface: Being too weak to tip something over.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses share four letters only because the apostrophe is dropped, which is standard in a grid. A canted camera angle and a canted deck are both leaning ones.
annotation.definitionFit: Lack the strength -> CANT: as can't, the everyday way of saying you are unable; and to cant is to tilt or lean over, the builder's and sailor's word.

entries.clue: Cheeky Irish always cutting payment to landlord (10)

indicatorNotes.cutting: something cutting into a thing goes right into the middle of it, so the letters named last land inside the ones before

blocks.note: Ir. is the dictionary's short form for Irish
what a tenant hands the landlord is rent
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

annotation.surface: Irish tenants forever trimming what they hand over to the landlord.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as reducing the rent and means slicing into a word instead. Irreverence is cheek aimed at whatever other people hold sacred, the word built on reverence.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheeky -> IRREVERENT: both describe a want of due respect, the irreverent kind directed at what others treat as solemn.
